.. _const-vendor-pairing:

Const-Vendor Pairing
---------------------

**Every module under** :mod:`pcapkit.const` **is generated by a matching crawler
under** :mod:`pcapkit.vendor`, with no exception. A registry copied from an IANA,
IETF or similar web-published table is never hand-maintained -- the crawler
re-scrapes the source and regenerates the module, so a hand edit to the generated
file is silently discarded on the next run. :issue:`2441`, raised in cross-review
and knowingly deferred rather than fixed.

The ``DATA`` Attribute, for a Registry With No Web Source
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

A source that is not a web-crawlable table does not excuse a module from this
pairing -- it changes what the crawler fetches. :class:`~pcapkit.vendor.default.Vendor`
reads its registry two ways: :meth:`~pcapkit.vendor.default.Vendor._request` either
``GET``\ s :attr:`~pcapkit.vendor.default.Vendor.LINK`, or, when a subclass overrides
:meth:`~pcapkit.vendor.default.Vendor.request` to take no arguments, returns a
module-level ``DATA`` literal instead and never touches the network.
:mod:`pcapkit.vendor.ipx.packet` and :mod:`pcapkit.vendor.ipx.socket` are the
precedent: both read a hand-transcribed ``DATA`` dict because their source,
Novell's and Xerox's own IPX socket/packet-type tables, went offline (:issue:`507`,
:issue:`518`).

:class:`~pcapkit.const.linux.arphrd.ARPHRD` follows this pattern: its source is the
Linux kernel header ``<linux/if_arp.h>``, C source
under the kernel's own versioning rather than an IANA page, so
:mod:`pcapkit.vendor.linux.arphrd` reads a ``DATA`` dict of
``{code: (name, description)}`` transcribed from the header instead of fetching a
URL. The crawler's :meth:`~pcapkit.vendor.default.Vendor.process` renders that dict
into the same enumeration members, the same ``FLAG`` bound and the same
``_missing_`` body the committed :mod:`pcapkit.const.linux.arphrd` carries --
running it is a no-op against the file in the tree, exactly as a web-scraped
crawler's run is. The explanatory prose that once lived in the hand-maintained
``const`` module -- which values are listed and why, the cross-reference to
:class:`~pcapkit.const.arp.hardware.Hardware` -- now lives in the crawler's own
module docstring and comments, alongside the ``DATA`` literal it documents; the
generated ``const`` module carries only the plain, templated docstring every
other generated module does.

Known Violation
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

:class:`~pcapkit.const.tls.content_type.ContentType` and
:class:`~pcapkit.const.tls.handshake_type.HandshakeType` (:pr:`2441`) both cite a live
IANA registry and claim to name every value IANA assigns, with no
:mod:`pcapkit.vendor` crawler behind either one -- no ``pcapkit/vendor/tls/``
directory exists, and neither class appears in :data:`pcapkit.vendor.__all__`. This
was flagged in that PR's own review and merged anyway on the stated reasoning that the
crawler would follow later. Tracked as :issue:`2495`. Unlike ARPHRD, TLS's source
*is* a live, web-published IANA table, so its eventual crawler takes the normal
``LINK``-and-scrape shape, not the ``DATA`` attribute.
